- Its angular size is normal, with the distance having little practical effect.

The main difficulty is locating it. Its azimuth, **193°**, places it roughly **13° west of due south**, very high overhead—about **58° above the horizon**. Look toward the south-southwest, well above the horizon, not near the Sun in the east-southeast.

Under the stated clear conditions, an ordinary observer would likely spot it within a few minutes, especially by using the app to guide the initial search. It may be less obvious if there are thin high clouds, haze, glare, or nearby obstructions, but the geometry is quite favorable.
